bt_static_sprite: Static sprite prop in Tower of Babel. Non-interactive decorative sprite for scene dressing.
btDC_plane_jumping:
Plane jumping scene — Neil flies Will to the tower.

Cutscene (~92 lines). Neil: "We'll be there soon, Will.
Say hello to your father for me." Will: "Thanks. I know you
mean that." The airplane approach and Will's jump into
the tower. Emotional farewell with Neil.
btDE_kara_missing:
Kara as the follower of Will in the Tower of Babel (placed in scenes $DE, $DF, $E0, $E1 and $E3). It dies at load when $D4 (Kara follows Will) is clear. In scene $E0 with $0178 set (the Neo Fanger fight was won) it clears $D4, locks the player, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), prints 'Kara's not here... Where did she go...?', unlocks and dies. Otherwise it spawns EscortFollowPathTracker at the player's position, follows the player and spawns the effect sprite code_09870C each time bit $2000 of the player's field $0E changes state.

$D4 is set by btDF_kara (scene $DF) and by btE3_kara (scene $E3).
btDE_monologue:
Will's monologue entering the Tower of Babel.

Narration: "The Tower of Babel was deathly quiet. Time stood
still..." Also: "The Flute I had was discovered here."
Atmospheric text establishing the tower's eerie silence.
Plays once on first entry.
btDE_olman:
Will's father Olman at the Babel entrance — emotional reunion.

Major story scene (~118 lines). "One worn-out body is quietly
laid down... In his head, a familiar voice speaks. Will.
It's me..." Will: "Father! Why are you in that form!!!"
Olman explains the strange room in the tower. Pivotal
reunion that drives the endgame plot.
btDF_crystal_ring:
Crystal Ring discovery in the Babel lower floors.

Event item (~138 lines): "Something seemed to fall from the
Flute..." Then: "It's King Edward's Crystal Ring!! I thought
it was a decoration, but it had been hidden there."
Key plot item connecting Edward Castle to the tower's secrets.
btDF_kara:
Kara in the Babel lower floors — fears permanent separation.

Emotional NPC (~82 lines). "Wait..." Then: "Will: Kara!!!?
Kara: I'm sorry. I just feel that, if we part now, we'll
never meet again..." Kara's fear drives her to follow Will.
Character moment before the final ascent.
btDF_spirits:
Tower spirits in the Babel lower floors — time distortion lore.

Multi-spirit NPCs (~88 lines). "The light released from the
comet has a profound effect on the growth of living things."
Also: "The passage of time is different inside the Tower
of Babel... Time races by..." Exposition about the tower's
temporal anomalies and the comet's biological effects.
btE0_crystal_gate_a: Crystal gate A of the Babel middle floors (scene $E0): marks the cells (71,38) and (72,38) solid, spawns two bt_static_sprite crystals and waits for $0175, which btF2_neo_castoth (scene $F2) sets when the Neo Castoth fight is won. It then clears the two cells and dies.
btE0_crystal_gate_b: Crystal gate B of the Babel middle floors (scene $E0): marks the cells (0D,28) and (0E,28) solid, spawns two bt_static_sprite crystals and waits for $0176, which btF3_neo_viper (scene $F3) sets when the Neo Viper fight is won. It then clears the two cells and dies.
btE0_crystal_gate_c: Crystal gate C of the Babel middle floors (scene $E0): marks the cells (49,18) and (4A,18) solid, spawns two bt_static_sprite crystals and waits for $0177, which btF4_neo_female_vampire (scene $F4) sets when the Neo Vampires fight is won. It then clears the two cells and dies.
btE0_crystal_gate_d: Crystal gate D of the Babel middle floors (scene $E0): marks the cells (15,08) and (16,08) solid, spawns two bt_static_sprite crystals and waits for $0178, which btF5_neo_fanger (scene $F5) sets when the Neo Fanger fight is won. It then clears the two cells and dies. The gate waits on its own flag only. $0178 is also read by btDE_kara_missing.
btE1_comet_soon:
Comet arrival warning in the light elevator area.

Extended NPC (~133 lines): "The comet will soon be entering
Earth's orbit. We must go to the top of the Tower of Babel..."
Urgent story exposition driving the player toward the
final confrontation.
btE1_light_elevator:
Light elevator mechanism in the Tower of Babel (~90 lines).

Automated elevator that carries the player upward using
a beam of light. Handles player attachment, vertical
movement, and the visual light shaft effect. Unique
transport mechanic for the tower.
btE2_brought_back: Spirit at the Babel exterior (scene $E2): a solid NPC with the interact handler 'You were brought back to save Earth. I'll take you to the top floor.', which sets scratch $01. The main script waits for $01 and then locks the player ($CFFC), moves to the player, spawns the child code_099899, hands the player the script btE1_comet_soon.code_0997B7 (the ride), sets bit $0800 of the player's flags, rises while y is at least $90, waits 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), moves to (0188,0110), kills the child, sets scratch $04 (read by the ride script) and unlocks. The actor tests no persistent flag.
btE3_crystal_gate: Crystal gate of the Babel upper floors (scene $E3): marks the cells (29,38) and (2A,38) solid, spawns two bt_static_sprite crystals and waits for $0179, which btF6_neo_queen (scene $F6) sets when the Neo Queen fight is won, just before it queues scene $E3. It then clears the two cells and dies.
btE3_dao_travel_spirit:
Dao travel spirit in the Babel upper floors — point of no return.

Offers return travel: "If you proceed, you will not be able
to turn back... If you want to go to Dao, I'll transport you."
Last chance to return to Dao before the final boss. Serves
as the point-of-no-return warning.
btE3_kara:
Kara in the Babel upper floors — concerned about the vampire woman.

NPC. Will: "Kara! Where did you go?!" Kara: "There was talk
that the vampire woman had come..." Kara's reason for
wandering off. Story continuity with the Mu vampires.
btE4_kara:
Kara on the Tower of Babel rooftop — the climactic fusion.

Major endgame scene (~190 lines). Kara: "..............." Then:
"When Will and Kara joined and became one with the Light
Knight, a great power was born..." The climactic moment
where Will and Kara merge with the Light Knight to
confront Dark Gaia. The game's emotional peak.
btE4_olman:
Olman on the Tower of Babel rooftop — final exposition (~257 lines).

The game's largest exposition scene. Will's father explains:
"The ancients worshipped the comet as a spirit. Those who
bathed in the comet's light..." Covers the comet's cyclical
return, the ancient civilization's evolution and corruption,
and the true nature of Light and Dark Gaia. Essential lore
for understanding the game's mythology.
CollisionLayerRenderer:
Collision layer tile renderer for the Pyramid trap rooms.

Technical actor (~116 lines) that draws the collision layer
tiles visible in the Pyramid's trap corridors. Reads collision
data and renders walkable/hazard tiles as visible sprites,
allowing the player to see which tiles are safe to walk on.
CreditPositionLookup: Credit text position lookup table. Maps staff credit entries to screen X/Y positions during the credits roll.
crF7_credits_camera_pan:
Credits camera pan controller (~195 lines).

Manages the smooth camera scrolling during the end credits
town walkthrough. Pans across the revisited locations as
character farewells play. Coordinates movement speed and
timing with the credits text display.
crF7_credits_dma_scroll:
Credits DMA scroll effect (~130 lines).

Handles hardware DMA-based background scrolling for the
credits sequence. Manages the tilemap scroll that reveals
the credits text as it rolls up the screen.
crF7_credits_hdma_flicker:
Credits HDMA flicker effect.

Subtle screen brightness pulsing via HDMA during the
credits. Creates gentle lighting transitions between
credit scenes.
daC3_babel_travel_spirit: Travel spirit of Dao (scene $C3, tile (21,08)). The actor dies at spawn while $D2 is clear (set by the Tower of Babel entrance monologue). With $D2 set it stands solid and asks 'Go to Tower of Babel?' with two rows (labelled 'Quit' and 'Return'); rows 0 and 1 of the handler table only clear the dialog; row 2 clears the dialog, zeroes $066D and $0670, sets gfxCacheIdxA and gfxCacheIdxB and queues scene $E3 at (0280,01B0).
dark_rewards:
Unused Dark Space reward actors (dark_rewards1, dark_rewards2, dark_rewards3).

Prototype reward dispensers that hint at abilities and stat boosts.
Likely an earlier version of the Dark Space ability system before
it was integrated into sE6_gaia. Never referenced by any scene.
ec_proximity_door_toggle:
Proximity-based door open/close actor used across Edward Castle.

Monitors player distance and toggles door tile state.
Shared utility actor used by multiple castle rooms.
ec0E_lily:
Lilly's first appearance in the aqueduct lockway (scene $0E, tile (3D,0E)).

Flag $DE set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise, when Will comes within #01 tile, it sets $DE, spawns an orbiting orb (code_09A9A1: hittable, 'Hey! What are you doing!!' when hit), moves for #$04B0 ticks by the direction DirToPlayer returns, prints 'Come here, or the demon will get you!' and moves away (moveXAlt $60, moveYAlt $30). It gives no puzzle guidance and has a single appearance, not multi-state dialog.
ec11_aqueduct_blocker:
Second switch-shaped hit target of the aqueduct doorway (scene $11, tile (03,07)).

Solid and unkillable (HP $FF); when hit it plays frames #11 and #12 and re-arms. It reads and writes no flag and has no effect on the door: only ec11_button_voice opens it.
ec11_aqueduct_gate_sprite:
One-shot orb sprite of the aqueduct doorway (scene $11, tile (0B,0B)).

Flag $DF set: dies at spawn. Otherwise it sets $DF, plays frame #33 of spriteset_pickups_effects for #02 steps and moves with StageMove / TickMove toward moveXAlt $0048, moveYAlt $0050. It has no open or closed gate state; the doorway door is the BG change #13 applied by ec11_button_voice.
ec11_button_voice:
The doorway switch of the aqueduct (scene $11, tile (1C,07), the same tile as ec11_countdown): a solid, unkillable hit target (HP $FF) with a hit callback.

Hit with word flag $0113 set or scratch $02 clear: plays frames #11 and #12 only. Hit with $02 set and scratch $01 set (the countdown's '3' window): clears $02, applies BG change #13 (the door), sets $0113, plays sounds and prints 'Stop! The door is open!! Go in!!'. Hit with $02 set and $01 clear: prints 'Wait! I told you, you have to push them at the same time!', then the voice's instructions again, and sets scratch $03, which restarts the count. The strange voice that counts is ec11_countdown; $02 is set by UseItem_LolaMelody_Effect.
ec11_countdown:
The strange voice of the aqueduct doorway (scene $11): an invisible actor at tile (1C,07).

Parks when word flag $0113 is set. Otherwise it waits for scratch $02 (set when Lola's Melody is played in this scene) and, when Will is within #03 tiles, locks the joypad, prints the instructions ('The door won't open unless you push this switch on the count of three'), starts music #1B, unlocks and counts: #$78 silent passes, sound #10 with digit 1 for #$3C, #$78 silent, sound #10 with digit 2 for #$3C, #$63 silent, then sets scratch $01 (the on-time window), sound #11 and digit 3 for #$28 passes, clears $01 and prints 'Wait! I told you ...'. A hit before the window sets scratch $03 (from ec11_button_voice), which restarts the count; the hit in the window opens the door and clears $02, which parks this actor.
ec11_flower:
Flower NPC in the aqueduct doorway.

Tells Will to play the Flute melody. Part of the melody-gated
progression system.
ec12_aqueduct_dark_space:
Dark Space portal in the aqueduct back area.

Spawns the dark space portal after flag check.
ec12_aqueduct_enemy:
Hit-toggle prop of the aqueduct back area (scene $12, tile (2B,56)); it uses the switch stats (HP $FF) and never dies.

Each hit plays frame #11; the first hit (word flag $0114 clear) also plays a sound, applies BG change #14, sets $0114, applies BG change #15 and sets $0115 (event blocks $14 and $15); later hits do nothing more. For form 0 (characterForm = 0) it first sets bit $0200 of $10.
ec13_lily:
Lilly at the aqueduct exit (scene $13, tile (07,08)).

Flag $3A clear: after WaitByte #01, music #1B and WaitByte #3B she waits; if Will is in another form (characterForm not 0) she first locks the joypad, prints 'When the enemies are destroyed, Will can return to his original shape...' and starts Transform_FreedanToWill on the player. When Will comes within #03 tiles she sets $3A, locks the joypad and prints 'Girl: I saw you!! ... You can change your shape like me! I'm Lilly, an Itory girl protected by the Flower Spirit' (Will learned the melody from Grandma Lola, who asked her to rescue him), plays a sound, prints 'The Elder is calling... I have to go. We'll meet again! Goodbye, Will!', walks away, unlocks and dies. The two do not set out together here.

Flag $3A set: she dies at spawn (the form revert still runs when needed).
hint_npc:
Unused hint NPC actors (hint_npc1 through hint_npc8).

Prototype Gaia-like hint dispensers that display dialog based on
scene flags. Similar to the hint system in sE6_gaia but standalone.
Never referenced by any scene.
ir1C_kara:
Kara at the Incan Ruins entrance — chases after the party.

Before flag $4B: waits for player to reach tiles (1A,0F)-(1B,11),
then locks joypad, plays music #1B, Kara walks in from the side
and scolds Will for leaving her behind. Two dialog states: initial
scolding, then asks if he found what he was looking for.
After flag $4B: repositions and waits with different dialog.
ir1C_lily:
Lilly at the Incan Ruins entrance (scene $1C): one escort scene in two states.

Flag $4B clear: she locks the joypad ($CFFC), waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), prints the entrance dialog (the Elder's story of the Incan Gold Ship), marks tiles (06,19) and (07,19) solid, unlocks, spawns EscortFollowPathTracker and polls scratch flag $01. When ir1C_kara sets $01 she kills the tracker, clears both solid tiles, waits for scratch $03, faces the player, prints the Lilly and Kara dialog (09CCD0), sets scratch $02 and waits for it to clear. Then she walks, prints the Elder-quote dialog (the statue on the Larai Cliff), sets $4B and unlocks the joypad.

Flag $4B set at spawn: she stands at tile (16,13), solid, with the Elder-quote dialog as her talk handler. When characterForm is not 0 (Will) she also sets the player actor's code pointer to sE6_gaia.Transform_FreedanToWill and sets playerFlags bit $0800. The file has no Dark Space or scene $4C code.
ir1D_bones:
Ground object hint on Larai Cliff — gold statue clue.

Solid interactable prop. When examined: "There's something on the
ground there... If I can move that gold statue, I can pass..."
Hints that the player needs to push the gold statue to proceed.
ir1D_wind_melody:
Wind Melody event at Larai Cliff (scene $1D).

With flag $32 set at spawn the actor dies. Otherwise it polls BranchIfPlayerAt for the exact pixel (0050,0170). On a match it locks the joypad ($EFFC), waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), starts music #1B, waits 120 ticks (WaitByte #77), plays sound #16 on channel 1, prints 'The wind in the valley plays a melody. The statue seems to be singing...', starts music #1A, waits 120 ticks (WaitByte #77) and then polls APUIO1 until it reads $FF. Then it calls GiveItem #08 (Wind Melody): on success it prints 'You've learned the Melody of the Wind!' and sets $32; with a full inventory it prints the 'inventory is full' text and leaves $32 clear, so the event repeats on the next visit. Both paths unlock the joypad and die.
ir1E_cliff_mantel_a:
Statue prop on the Larai Cliff back side, variant A (mantel tiles $37-$38, $12-$13; scene row at tile (37,14)).

Spawns hidden (the third actor-def byte #30 sets $2000 in $10), nudges its position by (08,FE), sets sprite priority #30 and waits with WaitOnFlagByte(#30, #01). When flag $30 (Incan Statue A placed on the mantel by UseItem_IncaStatueA) is set it clears $2000 in $10, which shows the statue sprite, and idles. With the flag already set at scene load the wait passes at once.
ir1E_cliff_mantel_b:
Statue prop on the Larai Cliff back side, variant B (mantel tiles $26-$27, $15-$16; scene row at tile (26,17)).

Same script as variant A with flag $31 (Incan Statue B placed on the mantel by UseItem_IncaStatueB): it spawns hidden, waits with WaitOnFlagByte(#31, #01), then shows the statue sprite and idles. Sprite priority #30.
ir1E_cliff_slide_trigger:
Cliff slide event of the Larai Cliff back scene ($1E).

Until flags $30 and $31 (both Incan statues on their mantels) are set, it runs every frame: SetFlagByte #00 while playerYPos is below $0110 and ClearFlagByte #00 otherwise (scratch flag $00, read by the player's idle sprite code). When both flags are set it sets scratch $00 for good, plays sound $1616 and polls BranchIfPlayerAt for the exact pixels (01E8,0120) and (01E7,0120). On a match it locks the joypad ($EFFC), plays sound $1616, spawns 40 debris helpers (LoopStart #28 passes, one every 9 ticks (JumpAfterDelay #$0008); code_09C51B starts each at X $02A0, Y $0090 plus a random byte and moves it along X, then dies), writes $FFF8 to playerSpeedEw, unlocks the joypad, waits 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B) and polls again.
ir1F_gold_tile:
Gold floor tile of the four-plate puzzle in scene $1F. Four copies; the spawn parameter bytes #03, #05, #07 and #09 give the actor word $0E = 1, 2, 3, 4.

With flag $3C set at spawn it dies. Otherwise it nudges its position by (08,08) and tests every frame BranchIfPlayerNear(#01) and BranchIfActorNear(slot, #01) for the actors in slots #02-#05 of the scene's actor list (the four stone lords), each with radius 1. When nothing stands on the tile it calls flag_helpers.ClearFlagRaw with A = $0E; when something does it calls flag_helpers.SetFlagRaw with A = $0E, so each tile owns scratch flag $01-$04. The first time the player steps on a tile in a visit it prints 'Stepping on a gold tile emits a sound. There are four gold tiles. Stand on each of the four tiles at the same time.' (latched by scratch flag $0F). ir1F_plate_gate_opener reads eventFlags AND $001E (bits 1-4) to see that all four tiles are occupied.
ir1F_plate_gate_opener:
Plate gate opener — opens passage when all 4 gold tiles are activated.

Checks flag $3C. Each frame, reads eventFlags AND $001E — when
all 4 tile bits are set (result = $001E), plays chime SFX ($0F0F),
applies BG change #08 to open the gate, sets flag word $0108
and flag $3C. Once opened, stays open permanently.
ir24_glowing_tile:
Glowing floor tile puzzle in the Inca plate room — timed step counter.

Checks flag word $0112. Starts a 600-frame countdown (orbitAngle =
$0258). Each frame checks if the player is standing in a specific
tile rectangle (14,17 to 17,1A). While player is on the tile, the
counter decrements. When it reaches 0, plays chime SFX ($0F0F)
and completes the puzzle step.
ir25_block_slot:
Block slot of the Incan Ruins entryway (scene $25), scene row at tile (0E,1C).

Spawns hidden (the third actor-def byte #23 sets $2000 in $10) and nudges its position by (08,00). With flag $2F (the Blue Block was fitted into the slot by UseItem_DiamondBlock_Place) set at spawn it runs code_09C3B3: it clears $2000 in $10, which shows the block, and idles. With $2F clear it waits with WaitOnFlagByte(#2F, #01), plays sound #2C on channel 2 and then runs the same show-block code.
ir25_ceiling_tile:
Falling ceiling tile of the Incan Ruins entryway (scene $25). Six copies at tiles (08,1A), (08,1C), (08,1E), (0A,1A), (0A,1C), (0A,1E).

Spawns hidden (the third actor-def byte #23 sets $2000 in $10) and nudges its position by (08,00). With flag $2F (the Blue Block was fitted into the slot by UseItem_DiamondBlock_Place) set at spawn it runs code_09C38D at once: it shows the tile, sets sprite priority to the minimum, clears collision on its tile, releases the joypad bits $CFFC and idles. With $2F clear it waits with WaitOnFlagByte(#2F, #01). When the flag turns on it locks the joypad ($CFFC), waits 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), plays sound $1515, spawns camera_drift.CameraDriftLoopSimple for screen shake, waits 180 ticks (WaitByte #B3), stores a random byte in $08, yields once, subtracts $100 from its Y, shows the tile, sets the priority to the maximum and falls (StageSpriteLoopMoveY #18, #02, #0F). On landing it plays sound $1515, ends on frame #35 and runs code_09C38D.
ir26_bones:
Explorer skeleton in the Inca treasure room — charm with family letter.

Solid interactable prop. When examined, shows a multi-page dialog:
"An explorer who sought the Incan Gold Ship..." then reveals a
charm containing notes from family members Nana and Sabas, asking
their father to return alive and buy a Kruk.
ir26_journal_bones:
Explorer skeleton with journal — hints at Melody of the Wind puzzle.

Solid interactable prop. When examined, shows a journal about
deciphering the Incan Melody of the Wind and the clue:
"Chant in the Golden Room. Does that mean to play the Melody
of the Wind...?" This hints at the Wind Melody puzzle solution.
ir28_bones:
Explorer skeleton in the ceiling trap room — flavor text object.

Solid interactable prop. When examined, displays: "An explorer who
sought the Incan Gold Ship...? He lost his life in a trap..."
ir28_ceiling_trap_trigger:
Ceiling trap controller of scene $28 (Incan Ruins ceiling trap room).

Invisible actor that polls six BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles rectangles every frame: (1A,0C)-(1C,0E), (1A,16)-(1C,18), (12,24)-(14,26), (08,24)-(0A,26), (10,1C)-(12,1E) and (12,16)-(14,18). Each rectangle has its own latch, scratch flag $01-$06 (set on entry and zeroed at every scene load, so a zone fires once per visit). A zone that fires spawns falling-tile helpers of ec_proximity_door_toggle at absolute pixel positions with SpawnAfterAbsFlags: zones 1-3 spawn one code_09C2DB helper each ((01A8,0130), (01C8,01C0), (00E8,0260)); zones 4-6 spawn two code_09C2E4 helpers each, with a WaitByte #0E between them ((0088,0220) and (0088,0200), (0088,01C0) and (0088,01A0), (0128,0160) and (0128,0140)). code_09C2DB marks the landing tile solid and code_09C2E4 clears its collision. After every zone check the actor plays sound $2C2C and polls again.
ir29_transform:
Aftermath actor of the Castoth fight (scene $29, scene row ;04).

With flag word $011F set at spawn it dies. Otherwise it waits until enemiesRemaining ($0AEC) is 0, locks the joypad ($EFFC), applies BG change #1F, sets $011F, fades to music #1B and waits 120 ticks (WaitByte #77). When characterForm is 0 (Will) it only unlocks the joypad. For any other form it locks the joypad ($CFFC), waits 90 ticks (WaitByte #59), prints 'After the demon disappears, Will returns to his original shape...', unlocks, sets the player actor's code pointer to sE6_gaia.Transform_FreedanToWill, sets playerFlags bit $0800, waits until that bit clears and unlocks the joypad ($EFFC).
it1A_moon_tribe:
Moon Tribe encounter at their camp.

Major story scene: the Moon Tribe introduces themselves as
Shadows created by the comet's light. Exposition about the
comet, the transformation, and Shadow's origin. Complex
multi-phase dialog with cutscene elements.
sF0_class_dismissed:
Class dismissed — the game's final scene (~208 lines).

Returns to South Cape school where the game began.
"Class is over. Please be careful crossing the street."
Will walks out of school into the sunlight. The bookend
moment that closes the game's narrative loop. Includes
the mysterious final encounter on the street.
sF7_credits:
Main credits sequence orchestrator (~822 lines).

The game's full end credits controller. Displays:
"The Illusion of GAIA — STAFF" followed by "Original Story:
MARIKO OHARA" and all development credits. Coordinates
NPC farewell appearances, location revisits, music changes,
and the player character's final walkthrough. The second
largest script in the game after Dark Gaia.
sF7_credits_misc_timeline:
Credits miscellaneous timeline events (~300 lines).

Coordinates timed events during the credits: camera
transitions, palette changes, special effect triggers,
and scene switches between revisited locations.
The timeline backbone for the credits sequence.
sF7_credits_npc_a:
Credits NPC group A — first farewell characters (~211 lines).

First batch of NPCs appearing during the credits walkthrough.
Each character plays a brief farewell animation or poses
as Will passes by. South Cape and early-game characters.
sF7_credits_npc_b:
Credits NPC group B — mid-game farewell characters (~155 lines).

Second batch of credits NPCs. Characters from Freejia,
the Gold Ship, and other mid-game locations.
sF7_credits_npc_c:
Credits NPC group C — later farewell characters (~113 lines).

Third batch from Watermia, Euro, and other locations.
sF7_credits_npc_d:
Credits NPC group D — late-game farewell characters (~95 lines).

Fourth batch from Dao, the Pyramid area, and beyond.
sF7_credits_npc_e:
Credits NPC group E — final farewell characters (~59 lines).

Last batch of NPCs. The Tower of Babel and ending-specific
characters.
sF7_credits_player:
Credits player character controller (~407 lines).

Manages Will's movement and animation during the credits
walkthrough sequence. Handles auto-walk paths, form
changes, idle poses at key locations, and the final
walk into the sunset. Complex movement scripting.
unused_debug_input_test:
Unused debug actor for cycling through enemy spriteset frames.

Advances frame index $28 on each A-button press (0..$32), displaying
one sprite from spriteset_pickups_effects per frame. Debug sprite viewer.
unused_debug_mode:
Unused debug initialization actor.

Sets player stats (HP=19, STR=32, DEF=33), character form to Shadow,
unlocks all abilities ($FF), sets MEMSEL fast ROM, flags the player
as dead ($0200), then enters the same sprite viewer loop as
unused_debug_input_test.
unused_kara_dialog:
Unused Kara dialog actor with looping music test.

Spawns a dialog child, alternates between music tracks #02 and #04
with a dialog prompt between each. Contains a single Kara dialog
line. Possibly a cutscene test or early Kara interaction prototype.
unused_mode7_boss:
Unused complete Mode 7 boss fight (~1,900 lines).

Full boss implementation with Mode 7 tilemap manipulation, orbital
attack patterns, HP tracking, phase transitions, projectile spawning,
and camera control. Uses ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef, hardware_math,
and enemy_stats_table. The largest unused code block in the ROM.
Possibly a cut boss or a prototype for the Babel Tower boss.
